records.Concise description: A historically important JavaScript/Node.js Bitcoin full-node and library implementation that demonstrated production-oriented alternative node architecture.
records.Deeper researched summary: bcoin is an alternative Bitcoin protocol implementation written primarily for JavaScript/Node.js with C/C++ components. Its documentation describes full-node, SPV, wallet, mining-backend, Layer-2-backend, and general library use cases. It was notable for bringing a full node into the JavaScript ecosystem and for production use at Purse.io. However, the canonical repository's last observed push was February 12, 2024, and the public documentation still leans on older Purse-era claims; no meaningful 2026 maintenance phase was verified.
records.Launch / history: Created in 2014 and later used as production infrastructure by Purse.io. The project website remains reachable, but current active maintenance was not verified in August 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is a durable example of Bitcoin full-node implementation diversity and browser/JavaScript-oriented protocol tooling without warranting presentation as a current peer to actively maintained node implementations.
records.Verification basis: First-party docs establish technical scope and historical use. GitHub metadata checked 2026-08-15 showed the canonical repository last pushed in February 2024; no current maintenance evidence was verified.
Research notes / uncertainties: Reachable documentation is not evidence of active maintenance.
Classified HISTORICAL rather than INACTIVE because the software has durable implementation-history value and the project has not clearly published a formal shutdown notice.
Do not repeat old Purse.io production claims as current deployment claims.

records.Concise description: Bitcoin's Lightning payment-channel network and its interoperable BOLT specification set, distinct from any single node implementation.
records.Deeper researched summary: The Lightning Network is a layer-two payment-channel network anchored to Bitcoin transactions, not a separate blockchain. Public Lightning nodes establish channels, exchange off-chain commitment updates, and route onion-encrypted payments according to interoperable protocol rules. The BOLT repository is a living specification process used by multiple implementations. Public graph data exposes announced nodes and channels, but private channels and off-graph activity mean public metrics do not represent total Lightning liquidity or economic activity.
Creators / founders: Joseph Poon and Thaddeus Dryja — authors of the original Lightning Network paper
records.Launch / history: The Lightning Network design was published in 2015. Multiple interoperable implementations reached Bitcoin mainnet in the following years, and BOLT specifications continue to evolve through active multi-implementation development.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is the canonical network/protocol layer that connects Lightning implementations, wallets, liquidity services, and payment infrastructure across MSC categories.
Important technical or cultural characte: Not part of Bitcoin consensus state
records.Verification basis: Primary Lightning paper and current BOLT specification repository establish protocol scope and active specification work.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call Lightning a blockchain.
Do not conflate Lightning Network protocol rules with LND, Core Lightning, Eclair, or LDK behavior.
Public channel count/capacity excludes private channels and does not equal total Lightning liquidity or economic activity.
Feature maturity must distinguish draft specification, implementation support, default behavior, and broad deployment.

records.Concise description: Lightning Labs' Go-based Lightning Network Daemon, a widely used full Lightning node implementation with gRPC/REST APIs and multiple Bitcoin chain backends.
records.Deeper researched summary: LND implements Lightning channel management, routing, payment forwarding, invoices, peer networking, and node APIs. It can connect to Bitcoin via bitcoind/Bitcoin Core, btcd, or Neutrino-style light-client backends depending configuration. LND is an implementation of the Lightning protocol rather than the protocol itself, and its feature set changes across releases. Current releases in 2026 confirm ongoing maintenance; feature claims such as splicing, offers, route blinding, Taproot Assets integration, or liquidity tooling should be dated to versions rather than treated as timeless Lightning properties.
Creators / founders: Lightning Labs and open-source LND contributors
records.Launch / history: Development began before Lightning mainnet launch; LND reached mainnet beta in 2018. LND 0.21.1-beta was released in June 2026 with continued 0.20.x maintenance releases in July 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the largest Lightning implementation families and a backend for many wallets, node platforms, payment systems, and operator tools.
Important technical or cultural characte: Watchtower support in the implementation family
Large ecosystem of node-management and wallet integrations
records.Verification basis: Current official repository, installation documentation, and 2026 release history establish active maintenance and implementation scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not present version-specific feature support as a property of all LND deployments.
Taproot Assets is a related Lightning Labs protocol/software stack, not synonymous with LND.
Wallets using LND remain WALLETS entities; node implementation stays canonical here.

records.Concise description: A C-based Lightning node implementation focused on protocol interoperability, performance, and extensibility through plugins.
records.Deeper researched summary: Core Lightning, formerly c-lightning, is an actively maintained Lightning implementation under the ElementsProject/Blockstream lineage. It depends on a Bitcoin backend and provides a plugin-oriented architecture that lets operators extend routing, liquidity, accounting, and application behavior without folding every extension into the core daemon. It has run on mainnet since the early Lightning production era. Specific support for offers/BOLT12, dual funding, splicing, onion messages, or related capabilities must be tied to current release documentation because the protocol and implementation evolve quickly.
records.Launch / history: The project began in 2015 as c-lightning and has been used on Bitcoin mainnet since 2018. It was renamed Core Lightning and remains under active development with repository commits observed on 2026-08-15.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It provides major implementation diversity in Lightning and is especially important for plugin-driven experimentation and spec-focused interoperability.
records.Verification basis: Current official repository activity and Blockstream/ElementsProject documentation establish active maintenance and canonical implementation scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Reverify specific BOLT12, dual-funding, splicing, and plugin capabilities before unqualified public feature copy.
Core Lightning is an implementation; do not use its behavior as a universal Lightning protocol claim.
